HSTU already provides a natural timestamp-aware mechanism: learned relative positional and bucketed temporal biases inside its SiLU attention, retaining the gated sequential-transduction backbone. The 2024 [HSTU paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.17152v3) establishes this design; [Scaling New Frontiers](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=e6pqwHR1Yh) reports ablations where relative-time information outperforms position-only bias. This supports testing elapsed-time structure, although it does not establish gains on the four fixed Amazon categories.

For multiple interest timescales, [Efficient Sequential Recommendation for Long Term User Interest Via Personalization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.03479), posted January 2026 and identified as ICDM 2025, compresses older histories into learnable tokens combined with recent interactions, explicitly supporting HSTU. It motivates jointly learned long-term context alongside recent interests, without independently fitted predictors.

A concrete experimental hypothesis: preserve HSTU and add per-head log-bucketed elapsed-time biases, optionally augmented with jointly learned short/medium/long decay scales inside the same attention layers. This specific combination is a proposal, not a verified published result. Enforce causal masking and derive temporal features solely from the observed prefix; never use the held-out target timestamp unless the inference interface explicitly supplies query time. Preserve final-nonpadding readout for left padding and identical timestamp handling in training and the embedded predictor. Compare against the corrected baseline using only the fixed macro validation HR@10 protocol, one trained checkpoint per category.
